blocks.text: A pending gene test never delays the cholangiogram, stopping lactose, nitisinone, cholic acid or intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). A result can remove the reason to operate; it can never supply a reason to wait (expert opinion; no guideline states it).

sub: Cholangiogram on the atresia timetable; send genetics the same day, in parallel.
Before the cholangiogram, look for Alagille syndrome: echocardiogram, spine film, eye exam for posterior embryotoxon (NASPGHAN/ESPGHAN 2017).
Stop lactose on suspicion. Send GALT activity before any red cell transfusion.
Succinylacetone is diagnostic; start nitisinone with the metabolic team without waiting for genes.
Low gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) with normal or low serum bile acids: send urine bile acids; oral cholic acid treats it.
High citrulline and galactose, fatty liver: lactose-free formula with medium-chain triglycerides (MCT).
Not genetic. Treat with IVIG ± exchange transfusion; no gene result is coming.
Known family variant only. EASL 2024 discourages it as a first test, except ABCB4 in small-duct primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC).
Listed genes only; misses newer genes and non-coding variants.
Ask whether copy-number (deletion/duplication) analysis is included.
Coding exons; misses most copy-number changes, non-coding variants, repeats and mitochondrial DNA.
Can be reanalyzed as new genes are published.
Coding and non-coding variants, copy number, mitochondrial DNA; more variants of uncertain significance (VUS) to sift.
Results in days: the test for the intensive care unit (ICU) and a pending transplant decision.
Copy-number gains and losses only; misses single-letter variants. Use when there are several anomalies or developmental delay.
Atresia pathway first; rapid trio genome or broad panel the same day.
Broad panel with deletion/duplication analysis, or trio exome. Add urine bile acids if GGT is low.
JAG1 and NOTCH2 with deletion analysis. Negative sequencing does not exclude Alagille syndrome.

items.t: Indeterminate or recurrent acute liver failure
sub: Rapid trio genome or exome. Do not wait for it if transplant criteria are met.

items.t: Older child, unexplained alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or cholestasis
sub: Exome with liver-focused analysis (ATP7B, ABCB4 and others).
Wilson disease: ceruloplasmin and urine copper first; ATP7B confirms.
Test only if cholestasis persists off PN: yield was 4.3% in this group (Togawa 2016).

blocks.text: SERPINA1 is not on every panel. Send a serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level and a Pi type (phenotype) or genotype in the first-line workup. The level rises with inflammation: if inconclusive, repeat it with a C-reactive protein (EASL 2024).

blocks.h: Yield depends on who is tested
items: 71% (22 of 31) when the phenotype looked genetic; 4.3% (2 of 46) with prematurity and other causes (Togawa 2016).
Open referral to US panels: 12% of 2,171 (Karpen 2021); 6.8% of 10,894 (Hoskins 2026).
Indeterminate pediatric acute liver failure: 37% of 260 by exome; 41% with onset in the first year; 64% when recurrent (Lenz 2024).
Acute liver dysfunction: rapid genome diagnosed 7 of 18 (Bonser 2023).
Infants under 1 year, same sample: rapid genome 49% vs targeted panel 27% (GEMINI, Maron 2023; yield included some VUS).

blocks.h: Use GGT to read the panel
items: Low or normal GGT: ATP8B1, ABCB11, TJP2, MYO5B, USP53; bile acid synthesis defects.
High GGT: JAG1, NOTCH2, ABCB4, CFTR, SERPINA1.
Limiting ATP8B1/ABCB11 sequencing to low peak GGT doubled the yield (18.8% to 35.1%) and missed no case (Wang 2016; one center in China).
Use GGT to interpret a result, not to refuse broad testing.
Whole-gene deletions, if the test did not include copy-number analysis (JAG1 especially).
Genes added after the panel was built (for example KIF12, USP53, ZFYVE19).
Deep intronic and promoter variants: exome capture misses them; consider genome or RNA studies.
Negative means negative for what was looked at, by the method used.
Trio testing doubled the odds of a diagnosis vs testing the child alone (odds ratio 2.04; Clark 2018).
Only parents can prove two recessive variants sit on different copies of the gene (in trans).
A new (de novo) dominant variant, such as in JAG1, is classified faster when both parents are negative.
Two variants in ABCB11 in the child alone is a hypothesis until the parents are tested.

head: Class
Do
rows: Act as diagnosed if the phenotype fits

sub: Test parents (phase) and affected and healthy siblings (segregation). EASL 2024 lists this as a route to upgrade a VUS.
BSEP or multidrug resistance protein 3 (MDR3) immunostaining on a biopsy; GGT and serum bile acids that fit the gene.
Urine bile acids, succinylacetone, citrulline, copper studies as the gene suggests.
A biopsy can help in suspected Alagille syndrome with a VUS (EASL 2024).
RNA or splicing studies, transport assays. In silico predictions are supporting evidence only.
41% of 1.69 million people tested carried at least one VUS; 80% of reclassified VUS became benign or likely benign (Chen 2023).
Mean 22 months for a VUS to be upgraded (Chen 2023).

blocks.h: When the gene changes the plan

sub: Alagille syndrome: avoid a Kasai unless atresia is still suspected. After a Kasai, transplant 47% vs 14% and death 32% vs 3% in matched patients (Kaye 2010).
Neonatal Dubin–Johnson syndrome: high conjugated bilirubin, near-normal transaminases; no surgery.
Citrin deficiency: no surgery; lactose-free MCT formula.
Low-GGT cholestasis: no surgery; the genotype guides drugs and biliary diversion.

Severe bile salt export pump (BSEP) deficiency: median native liver survival 3.5 years and liver cancer in 34% by age 15, vs 20.4 years and 4% with at least one p.E297G or p.D482G variant (BSEP1; van Wessel 2020).
EASL 2024: closer liver cancer screening, no surgical biliary diversion, consider early transplant.
Valproate is contraindicated: it can trigger fatal acute liver failure (FDA label). The neurological course weighs on transplant.

items.t: One ABCB4 or ABCB11 variant, or a VUS
sub: Not a diagnosis; at most a modifier. Never cancels or delays a cholangiogram.

blocks.text:
A negative exome is a draft. Reanalysis added a diagnosis in 10% pooled across 29 studies (Dai 2022). EASL 2024: reanalyze exome or genome data at least every 3 years. ACMG 2019 asks laboratories for a reanalysis policy but sets no interval, so in practice the clinician must ask.

Counseling comes before the test (EASL 2024). Agree in advance which incidental and secondary findings will be returned: a genome can report adult-onset actionable genes (ACMG secondary findings list v3.3, 2025).

Record the exact variant in the chart. It is needed for testing relatives and for any related living donor.

items.text: Yield reflects who was tested: 71% when the phenotype looked genetic, 4.3% with prematurity (Togawa 2016).
Exome and genome data can be re-read; a panel cannot.
Indeterminate acute liver failure was genetic in 37%, and in 64% when recurrent (Lenz 2024). Sequence before or alongside listing.
"Sequencing negative" without copy-number analysis: a whole-gene JAG1 deletion is missed, and Alagille syndrome gets a Kasai.
A VUS is not a diagnosis. Test relatives to resolve it (segregation), not to diagnose or clear them.
One heterozygous ABCB4 or ABCB11 variant does not explain an infant's cholestasis: 77.5% of one Taiwanese cohort carried at least one heterozygous variant in cholestasis panel genes (Chen 2019).
Genome for every cholestatic infant: in a preterm on PN the yield is low and VUS add anxiety without benefit.
